A [[Gender|male]] individual was the '''father''' of the [[human]] [[Kanan Jarrus|Caleb Dume]], later known as Kanan Jarrus. Although Jarrus did not remember his [[Parent|father]] due to being taken from his family by the [[Jedi Order]], he later thought about his father on multiple occasions in his adult life.

==Biography==
[[File:KananJarrus.png|thumb|right|170px|Kanan Jarrus never knew his father.]]
A [[Gender|male]] individual was the [[Parent|father]] of the [[human]] [[Kanan Jarrus|Caleb Dume]],<ref name="A New Dawn" /> a [[Homeworld|native]] of<ref name="SWR:TVG">''[[Star Wars Rebels: The Visual Guide]]''</ref> the [[planet]]<ref name="Timelines">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''</ref> [[Coruscant]]<ref name="SWR:TVG" /> who was [[Reproduction|born]] in [[33 BBY]].<ref name="Timelines" /> Dume was taken from his family at a [[Youngling|young age]] and [[Jedi training|trained]] as a [[Jedi]] and therefore never knew his father. Dume came to be known as Kanan Jarrus following the [[Order 66|fall]] of the [[Jedi Order]]<ref name="A New Dawn" /> in [[19 BBY]].<ref name="Timelines" /> When Jarrus ended up on the planet [[Gorse]]<ref name="A New Dawn" /> in [[12 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines" /> the [[miner]] [[Okadiah Garson]] kindly took him under his wing. At one point<ref name="A New Dawn" /> in [[11 BBY]],<ref name="Eleven">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of [[A New Dawn (novel)|''A New Dawn'']] to [[11 BBY]].</ref> while he [[Diet|ate]] [[stew]] in [[Drakka's Diner]], Jarrus pondered how the Jedi teachings regarding attachment had impacted his life as a fugitive, and his thoughts drifted towards his own father. After consideration of Garson's role in his life, he felt that the [[foreman]] was the most father-like patron he had met during his travels.<ref name="A New Dawn" />

During the [[Battle of Garel]]<ref name="Legacy" /> in [[3 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines" /> when Jarrus' [[Padawan|apprentice]] [[Ezra Bridger]] wanted to return to the planet [[Lothal]] to find [[Ephraim Bridger|his]] [[Mira Bridger|parents]], who he had presumed [[Death|dead]] until a recent [[Force vision]], Jarrus warned him to be cautious. Growing frustrated, Bridger angrily stated that Jarrus had no idea what he was feeling. Jarrus calmly responded by admitting that Bridger was right, noting he had never known his parents, causing Bridger to apologize for the comment.<ref name="Legacy" />

==Behind the scenes==
Kanan Jarrus' father was first mentioned in the [[2014]] novel [[A New Dawn (novel)|''A New Dawn'']], written by [[John Jackson Miller]].<ref name="A New Dawn" />
